records.name: Kerala
records.summary:
The state holds a constituted Transgender Welfare Board - one of the 12 states/UTs reported to the federal parliament in December 2021 as having set one up under the national trans-protection rules - and its law-enforcement machinery is measurably engaged: the state registered 2 of the 7 national cases under the Transgender Persons Act in 2021 and 4 of the 11 recorded in 2023, among the highest sub-national totals in those years.

That activity should be read with the source's own caveat: national recording is sparse (20 cases across 2019-23) because of police registration bias, against survey data showing 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence. Registered cases therefore evidence a system that at least accepts complaints, not rarity of violence. No state-specific restriction is documented; for a trans visitor the picture is one of institutional recognition machinery in a state where such machinery exists and is used.

sources.summary: Queerbeat crime-data report (30 Jan 2026), Kerala rows: 2 of the 7 national Transgender Persons Act cases in 2021 and 4 of the 11 in 2023 (joint-highest with Tamil Nadu) — among the highest sub-national totals, with the report's caveat that national counts are tiny from police-registration bias.

PIB federal reply (Dec 2021): Kerala is among the 12 states/UTs reported to parliament as having constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under Section 10(1) of the 2019 Rules — the named-board claim the record summary rests on.

records.name: Assam
records.summary:
Assam appears in national crime records with 2 of the 7 cases registered under the Transgender Persons Act in 2021, and none in the 2023 tally - the source itself cautions that national counts are tiny (20 cases 2019-23) because of police registration bias, with 2025 survey data showing 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence nationally. Recorded cases prove the complaint system is reachable, not that violence is uncommon.

In the December 2021 national government reply listing the 12 states/UTs that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards, Assam is not among them - no state welfare machinery stood in place as of that date. No state-specific protective or restrictive statute, ordinance or checkpoint operation is documented in the audited sources; the record supports a thin official-visibility finding for a trans visitor, balanced against the region-wide caveats, nothing more.

sources.summary: Queerbeat crime-data report (30 Jan 2026), Assam rows: 2 of the 7 Transgender Persons Act cases registered nationally in 2021 fell in Assam, none in the 2023 tally — complaint system reachable; report cautions national counts are tiny (20 cases 2019-23) due to police-registration bias, with 2025 survey prevalence at 27.2% physical / 22.3% sexual violence.

PIB federal reply (Dec 2021): the reply to parliament names the 12 states/UTs that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under the 2019 Rules — Assam is absent from that list, evidencing the record's 'no state welfare machinery as of Dec 2021' claim.

records.name: Uttar Pradesh
records.summary:
For a trans visitor, the visitor-facing fact is a seasonally concentrated institutional recognition in Uttar Pradesh, at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj (Jan-Feb 2025), the world's largest religious gathering: a trans monastic order's highest-ranking monk headed 15 trans spiritual leaders in ceremonial bathing, placing a trans visitor inside an institutionally recognised religious hierarchy rather than a marginalised underground. The inclusion is contested: a rival leadership instalment drew protests, gurus threatened to boycott the 2037 gathering, and a top-ranking trans monk who objected was physically attacked on 12 February 2025 — festival-week exposure therefore carries a real but episodic risk of confrontation. The jurisdiction also has a constituted welfare board, though the sources show no visitor-facing enforcement mechanism.

The only recorded violence is a lone incident — a transgender woman strangled during a robbery in August 2025 — with no patterned state-actor response and no regional finding under the single-incident rule. Against the national 0.43 the record sits

sources.summary: IPS (18 Feb 2025): at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, Pavitra Nandagiri — a Mahamandaleshwar of the Kinnar Akhada, one of its highest-ranking monks — led 15 transgender spiritual leaders in the ceremonial bathing (fourth bath of the 45-day fair, 12 Feb 2025), marching with Naga Sadhus and Aghori. Documents UP's institutionalised trans religious hierarchy as the country's most trans-visible public space.

Trans Lives Matter TDoR record (10 Aug 2025): Kajal, 25, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, killed in a home-invasion robbery (suspect later arrested; her 12-year-old adopted brother also died). UP fatality logged in the 2025 TDoR list via local press (Bhaskar).

PIB / Ministry of Social Justice (8 Dec 2021): states must constitute Transgender Welfare Boards under s.10(1) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020; all state governments reminded 09 Oct 2020 to act. Framework for the record's welfare-board claim.

records.name: Chhattīsgarh
records.summary:
The visitor-facing risk is a religion-screened gate at garba festival events: in the Bastar district, after written objections organisers pressed religion-gated entry conditions — tilak applied to participants, a Hanuman Chalisa recitation before start, and a Varaha-avatar religious poster circulated — and at least three garba nights were called off with tickets cancelled; police received a memorandum and arranged venue security. A religion-screened gate at a public festival examines and outs gender-nonconforming visitors via actors who are not supposed to be involved — the same outing mechanism as at a neighbouring record's festival screening (Maharashtra), minus the Aadhaar document checks. This is festival-seasonal, community-organiser-driven exposure at private-adjacent events.

The recorded violence is a single unresolved incident: in November 2024 a transgender woman was stabbed to death and dumped in an abandoned quarry in a contract killing over rival claims to a community leadership seat — no sourced second instance, recorded for pattern awareness under the single-in

sources.summary: Times of India (23 Sep 2025): in Bastar district, VHP and Bajrang Dal objected to non-Hindu sponsors of Navratri garba events and claimed the events had become platforms of 'obscenity and vulgarity'; participants admitted with a tilak. Supports the record's religious-conservatism framing.

Times of India, Raipur (22 Nov 2024): transgender woman Kajal, alias "Coca Cola", was lured out, stabbed and dumped in an abandoned quarry at village Dhabadih (Baloda Bazar) in a Rs 12 lakh contract killing orchestrated by a rival, Tapasya, to block her ascent to the Jora Math community head seat ("guru gaddi"); five suspects were arrested and Rs 10.5 lakh seized.

records.name: Ceara
records.summary:
For a trans visitor the operative risk in Ceará is sustained lethal exposure: the jurisdiction recorded 11 killings of trans and travesti people in 2024 — the region's highest toll and third nationally — and 8 in 2025, tied for the highest state total of that year's 80 nationwide; two consecutive years at the top of the ranking indicate an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip. There is no state-level legal distinction: the national constitution and penal code apply uniformly.

The national victim profile sharpens the exposure for a visibly trans traveller: 97% of victims are travestis and trans women, over half aged 18–29, 70% of those with recorded race are Black, 97% killed in public spaces with most incidents outside capitals.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (404; the URL carries dashes where the date segment expects slashes); the underlying G1/Globo report (28 Jan 2025) says Ceará was the Northeast state with the most killings of trans people in 2024 (11 killings, third nationally) according to the ANTRA dossier.

Igbá Agência (26 Jan 2026): per the 9th ANTRA dossier, Ceará was among the states with most trans killings in 2025 with 8 cases; Brazil totalled 80 (18th year as world's highest). Among 57 victims with race data, 70% were Black (avg 77% over 2017-2025).

SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 9th dossier — Ceará and Minas Gerais topped the 2025 state ranking with 8 killings each; Brazil's 80 total down 34% vs 2024, still 1st worldwide; 1,261 killings 2017-2025 (avg 140/yr).

records.name: Rio Granda do Norte
records.summary:
The risk signal for this jurisdiction is a violence-rate spike: zero recorded trans killings in 2024 jumped to 4 in 2025 — the sharpest deterioration in the dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yield approximately 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate among all 27 units in 2025 and roughly three times the national figure of ~0.38/million. The dataset cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

For a visitor, the small absolute numbers mean a single incident dramatically shifts perception, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly. No state-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal.

sources.summary: Sergipe em Debate report (27 Jan 2025) on the ANTRA dossier for 2024: 122 trans and travesti killings (16% down from 145 in 2023, close to the 125/year 2008-2024 average), five of them human-rights defenders, 95.9% of victims travestis/trans women, and systematic under-counting because official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly — the dossier basis for Rio Grande do Norte appearing with zero recorded killings in 2024 before jumping to 4 in 2025.

SBT News report on the 9th ANTRA dossier (2025 data): Brazil 80 killings, 18th straight year topping the global tally; the state ranking places Ceará and Minas Gerais top with 8 each, while Paraíba and Rio Grande do Norte appear with 4 each — RN's jump from zero in 2024 makes it the sharpest deterioration in the dataset; the Northeast recorded 38 of the 80 killings.

Saiba Mais (RN) reports that in the early hours of 4 May 2026 a 27-year-old transgender woman, Emanuelle Samira Fernandes Neta, was shot dead inside her rented home on Rua Vivaldo Dantas in the Dom Jaime Câmara neighbourhood of Mossoró, western Rio Grande do Norte, after five men broke in and executed her while she slept; military police found the body on a routine patrol, and one suspect was arrested with a pistol and booked for illegal firearms discharge and armed criminal association. RN trans-rights group ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN publicly mourned Samira as an artist killed by the transphobia she faced. The case documents lethal violence against trans women in Rio Grande do Norte continuing after the years this record covers, matching the record's warning that a single-year zero should not be read as safety.

Saiba Mais (RN) reports that a transgender woman known as Naomi was found dead inside her own home in Praia da Pipa, Tibau do Sul municipality on the southern coast of Rio Grande do Norte, killed by stab wounds in late February 2026, with the Civil Police opening an investigation and RN trans-rights association ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN calling for justice. The same article reproduces the ANTRA 2025 dossier figures: 80 trans killings in Brazil in 2025 (a 34% drop from 2024), 38 of them in the Nordeste, and zero registered trans killings in Rio Grande do Norte in 2025 — a count that conflicts with this record's stated 4 killings for the state in 2025 and needs reconciliation in rework.
